newsitem.title: USA: Missouri soy planting two weeks ahead of 1996 pace.
newsitem.headline: Missouri soy planting two weeks ahead of 1996 pace.

text.p: Soybean planting in Missouri during the week ended Sunday was two weeks ahead of the 1996 pace and 11 days ahead of the five-year average, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service weekly report.
Single-crop soybeans were 79 percent planted with the northwestern area the most advanced at 95 percent.
Corn was developing well and the crop condition was largely unchanged from the previous week with five percent excellent, 53 good, 38 fair and four poor.
Sorghum was 77 percent planted, one week ahead of last year and the five-year average of 67 percent.

Cotton was developing late with no fields squaring versus eight percent a year ago and the two percent average. The crop condition declined from the previous week with warm weather needed to improve growth. Cotton was rated one percent excellent, 44 good, 36 fair, 18 poor and one very poor.

Winter wheat condition decreased slightly to 64 percent good to excellent, 26 fair, nine poor and one very poor. Harvesting was expected to start this week in southern counties. The crop was 98 percent headed, about two days behind last year and the average. Forty percent had turned color, about three days ahead of last year and one day ahead of the average.
Topsoil moisture was rated 24 percent surplus, 64 adequate and 12 short. Many fields remain wet from heavy rains a week ago.
Pasture and range condition was rated four pecent excellent, 48 good, 38 fair, nine poor and one very poor.
